style: point the listener to one word to listen for

candidates.angle: Krishna maps the three gunas onto directions: upward, middle, and downward
candidates.evidence: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छन्ति... मध्ये तिष्ठन्ति... अधो गच्छन्ति...

candidates.angle: The word sattvastha means those established in sattva, and it points to the upward path
The word rajasa means those in rajas, and it points to the middle path

en.intro: Krishna offers a map of movement. Listen to how he pairs each guna with a direction.
en.notice: Krishna maps the three gunas onto directions. Sattva, sattvastha, means those established in sattva, and they move upward. Rajas, rajasa, means those in rajas, and they remain in the middle. Tamas, tamasa, means those in tamas, and they go downward.
en.next: Krishna then says that the seer who knows the one beyond the gunas reaches his own being.
en.meaning: Those established in sattva go upward; those in rajas remain in the middle; those in the lowest movement of tamas go downward.

hi.intro: कृष्ण गति का एक नक्शा देते हैं। सुनिए, वे कैसे हर गुण को एक दिशा से जोड़ते हैं।
hi.meaning: सत्त्वगुण में स्थित मनुष्य ऊर्ध्वलोकों में जाते हैं, रजोगुण में स्थित मनुष्य मृत्युलोक में जन्म लेते हैं और निन्दनीय तमोगुण की वृत्ति में स्थित मनुष्य अधोगति में जाते हैं।
hi.notice: कृष्ण तीनों गुणों को दिशाओं से जोड़ते हैं। सत्त्वस्था का अर्थ है सत्त्वगुण में स्थापित, और वे ऊपर जाते हैं। राजसाः का अर्थ है रजोगुण में रहने वाले, और वे बीच में रहते हैं। तामसाः का अर्थ है तमोगुण में रहने वाले, और वे नीचे जाते हैं।
hi.next: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि जो द्रष्टा इन गुणों के पार के दिव्य स्वभाव को जानता है, वह मुझ तक पहुँच जाता है।

en.intro: Krishna offers a map of movement. Listen to how he pairs each guna with a direction.
en.body: Those established in sattva go upward; those in rajas remain in the middle; those in the lowest movement of tamas go downward. Krishna maps the three gunas onto directions. Sattva, sattvastha, means those established in sattva, and they move upward. Rajas, rajasa, means those in rajas, and they remain in the middle. Tamas, tamasa, means those in tamas, and they go downward. Krishna then says that the seer who knows the one beyond the gunas reaches his own being.
